correctness.rationale: The genus-two canonical map h:C→P¹ is a degree-two map with K_C≅h*O(1). Every bicanonical divisor is F_s+F_t; a degree-three sub-divisor is exactly P+F_t. The Abel–Jacobi map Sym³(C)→Pic³(C) is a P¹-bundle because h⁰(L)=2 and h¹(L)=0 for every degree-three line bundle. The locus is the inverse image of the smooth Abel curve T={K_C(P)}. Multiplication by the canonical section of O_C(P) identifies H⁰(K_C) with H⁰(K_C(P)) and trivializes the restricted projective bundle. Adjunction on the abelian surface Pic³(C) gives N_T≅K_C, hence N_Q3≅p_C* K_C. The argument covers repeated and ramified fibers and uses no finite experiment.
risks: The argument relies on standard algebraic-geometric facts; the scope is limited to smooth genus-two curves in characteristic zero.
